items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: So I used to hang around George Gantt over and go get a profession on my banjo playing, you see? And he used to let me sit in a couple of while, see?

ctx.x: Why don't you let me ask the question? That's okay. I've already looked into your history a little bit. So you started playing at the Hall, what, probably in the mid-60s?

Well, the Hall had opened up a little bit, but if you had Larry Boyce, he'd open it up for pleasure. And when I came back in 1968 to Chicago, I don't know if that's the exact year. No, no, no, no, no. I'm sure I made a mistake there. It was before that. I had been in Chicago before. But anyhow, I wasn't playing guitar, so I wasn't interested in the music. I played in my younger days. So I used to hang around George Gantt over and go get a profession on my banjo playing, you see? And he used to let me sit in a…
Okay. When did you drop the, well, all right, so you started, when you came back from Chicago in 68, you started at the Hall?
